newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open lower on Dow and copper slumps.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open lower on Dow and copper slumps.

text.p: Australian shares opened weaker on Thursday as the market followed the Dow lower and the resources sector factoring in the continued slide in the price of copper.
At 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 15.2 points lower at 2,689.9.
The June share price index was down 14 points at 2,694 and at a 4.1 point premium to the underlying index.
Market turnover was boosted early by option exercises in National Australia Bank stock which went ex-dividend today, paying an interim dividend of 45 cents.
"Last night, 26,400 NAB call options were exercised by holders that wanted to lock in profits before the dividend payout," a dealer from Brisbane brokerage Lance Jones said.
The dealer said National Australia bank stock had risen substantially since its last dividend payment, meaning most call options bought since that time were in-the-money.
The industrial sector was impacted negatively by National Australia Bank's dividend payment and by the cyclical transport sector which was reflecting Wednesday's Dow pullback.
Resource sectors, with the exception of energy, also opened down with big miners feeling the effect of weaker metal prices.

Bellwether resources stock The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd opened weaker again ahead of its results on Friday. BHP shares were 15 cents weaker at A$19.10 (US$14.33). BHP has fallen 75 cents or 3.3 percent since its close at A$19.85 last Friday.
Energy stocks went against the weaker trend with oil and gas companies Santos and Woodside Petroleum both opening stronger after oil prices rose on Wednesday.
Crude oil futures prices settled higher in U.S. trading after OPEC oil ministers agreed to roll over their self-imposed production ceiling for six months starting July at a summer meeting in Vienna.
